newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firms, premiums pressured by supply.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firms, premiums pressured by supply.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices gained slightly on Monday in line with stronger IPE futures, but premiums were barely steady amid signs of increased supply of heating oil, traders said.
NOV IPE futures ended 25 cents firmer at $234.00 a tonne, helped by tight stocks in Europe and the United States and political instability in Russia.

Traders said heating oil supplies were growing but still below historical levels and most said those for diesel were still tight, resulting in additional sensitivity to supply factors and the onset of winter temperatures.
"No one is holding much (heating oil) at the refinery so if there is cold weather we'll get the big (price) boost we have been waiting for," one trader said.

Prompt cargoes of German winter grade (-7/-22) heating oil were offered at Nov IPE +$6/7, unchanged to slightly easier compared to Friday's levels. A cargo of Russian was traded at mean quotes cif NWE minus 50 cents.

One trader, dissenting from the majority view, said he saw additional quantities of low sulphur diesel coming to Europe from the U.S. and the Mediterranean. He valued intermediate grade diesel at Nov IPE +$26/29, up $2 from Friday.
